segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hi Dana, yeah, thanks for making time. I wanted to walk through the seat count and the March 15 go-live plan, then I can send the order form right after.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. We’re still at 84 users for launch. Finance asked if we can add 10 more in May without redoing the whole agreement.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. The order form will show 84 seats at $72 per seat per month, annual term, and then any added seats co-term to the November 30 renewal date. So if you add 10 on May 1, billing just prorates those seven months.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that’s clear. What’s the annual total on the 84?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It comes to $72,576 for the software, plus the one-time onboarding package at $4,800. Total first-year invoice would be $77,376, net 30.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That matches what I had. Can the invoice be split, half at signature and half on July 1?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can do two invoices: $38,688 due at signature and $38,688 due July 1. The pricing sheet already reflects that payment schedule, so the order form will match.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Legal had one small thing: they want auto-renewal removed, just a written renewal each year.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No issue. I’ll send it as a 12-month term ending November 30, 2026, no auto-renewal, and we’ll start renewal conversations at least 60 days before that.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. If you send that today, I can route it for signature tomorrow morning.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. You’ll have the order form and implementation summary by 2 p.m. Eastern, and the kickoff is still held for March 3 at 11 a.m. with your admin team.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Thanks, Mark. That should get us there.
